This stalwart and sturdy Corgi is here to join you on your adventures!

These models are designed for use with tabletop roleplaying games, such as Dungeons and Dragons or Pathfinder, but it is detailed enough to scale up and print as you please.

As is, it is scaled to fit on a 25.4mm / 1 inch round base, not included. The 3-Headed version is scaled for both Medium and Large bases, so print him as large and terrifying as you want!

Two versions of the four standard Corgis are provided: Heroic, and Small. Small is scaled to be close to 28mm accurate, and Heroic is scaled to be larger and easier to print. If you have any doubts as to which to choose, go for Heroic!

This model was made possible thanks to the support of https://beldolorstudios.com/ ! They commissioned it and allowed it to be uploaded and printed by all!

Please note that they own the sole commercial right to print and sell all versions of this model, and as such no commercial use other than through them is allowed, and no remixes are allowed.

Easy to print, FDM-friendly Pillbug (land isopods, roly-polys, etc) companions!

These are meant for tabletop roleplaying games such as D&D, Pathfinder, etc, but can be used for whatever you wish.

These giant fantasy isopods (don't at me about anatomy) are available in multiple flavors, including smooth, saddled, and cannoned.

The cannon prints separately (print the cannon oriented vertically with the mouth touching the build plate) and snaps into place, and includes a small prop crate of cannonballs.

They have been sized as Medium-sized (fits on a 1 inch / 25.4mm round base) creatures, but if you scale them up by about 150% they would work fine as Large creatures (Fits on a 2 inch / 50.8mm round base).

They print with minimal supports and should be quite sturdy, even with a 0.4mm nozzle.
They will look best printed in resin, or with a 0.2mm nozzle for fine details.
Example prints were printed at 0.16mm layer heights with a 0.4mm nozzle.

Simple supports will be needed on the cannon pivot points; be sure to cut or file down the contact point with supports.

From behind a dense copse of trees, a large shape trundles forth. It sniffs and bends down, broad nose pushing through the detritus of the forest floor, searching for something. Its dense, earthy fur is entwined with a dense mat of hyphae, and you're not entirely sure where it begins and ends, all seemingly connected to the odd collection of mushrooms fruiting over its body. It looks up, chewing absentmindedly on something, stopping suddenly as it notices your party. It eyes you warily, snorting loudly in your direction, before bolting back into the forest's depths, a dense cloud of spores swirling behind it.


This is what happens when hungry hogs start rooting around for fae-touched truffles over a few generations. Alternatively: Porkabello. Porcine Porcini?

This is a 28mm scale miniature, suitable for tabletop roleplaying games such as Dungeons and Dragons or Pathfinder. No base is supplied, but is scaled to fit on a medium sized base (25.4mm / 1 inch diameter).

This is a re-detailed remaster of an [earlier miniature](https://www.thingiverse.com/thing:3669594)!

"Rat Rogue! He's ready to plunder the nearest dungeon of loot, sack at the ready to haul it back in! Perfect for homebrew races like Ratfolk, Ratkin, etcetera."

My first sculpt was fairly early on in my Blender learning experience, and I like to think that I've improved a little bit since then, so I decided to add a little more detail to it. Some superfluous clothing folds, better looking belt pouches, a few details here and there, you get the idea. The earlier version looked fine printed with FDM, but now that I have a resin printer I've realized it needed a little more spice!
